title: Wanted: new chief justice
primary_topics: Systematic exposition of the eight unique functions of the chief justice not required of associate justices
Constitutional qualifications for the CJ: natural-born, 40 years old, 15 years legal practice or judgeship
CJ as the role model and last bulwark of democracy -- addressed as CJ of the Philippines, not just of the SC
sub_topics: Source: CJ's new book 'With Due Respect' (printed edition sold out; digital still available)
1. Primus inter pares -- presides over sessions, controls flow, shapes agenda, one vote, leads by moral ascendancy
2. Leader of entire judiciary -- CEO of 2,000 judges and 26,000 employees; jurist vs leader paradox
3. Passionate reformer -- passion for reforms, interaction with public/private offices, foreign governments, international institutions; automation and computerization
4. Leader of the bar -- Supreme Court supervises practice of law; lawyers look up to CJ for direction
5. Academic and maestro -- ex-officio chair of Philippine Judicial Academy; CJ as guru for continuing education of judges; outside assistance without compromising independence
6. Mover and shaker -- JBC chair; better compensation, security, facilities for judges to attract best and brightest
7. Administrator, manager and finance wizard -- constitutional administrative supervision over all courts; sole discretion over JDF and SAJ funds (PD 1949, RA 9227)
8. Role model and exemplar -- people look up to CJ as model upright public servant; civic groups during political wrangling
CJ more accurately 'Chief Justice of the Philippines', not just of the SC

stances.claim: The CJ's eight unique duties — not required of associate justices — collectively transform the office from the highest jurist to the leader and CEO of the entire third branch of government, making the CJ more accurately the 'Chief Justice of the Philippines' than merely 'Chief Justice of the Supreme Court.'
stances.rhetorical_move: taxonomic-expansion argument: eight-duty enumeration as proof of the CJ's institutional breadth beyond the judicial function

stances.claim: The CJ's exclusive sole power to disburse the Judiciary Development Fund and Special Allowances for the Judiciary — combined with administrative supervision over all courts and personnel — makes the administrator-manager-finance wizard dimension of the role constitutionally and legally robust, not merely informal.
stances.rhetorical_move: legal-authority enumeration: statutory and constitutional sources for the CJ's managerial power

notable_anecdotes: The cross-reference to CJ Panganiban's book 'With Due Respect' — printed edition sold out per Inquirer president Sandy Romualdez, digital version still available — used as the source for the eight-duty taxonomy, making the column itself a public excerpt from a book whose commercial success signals broad civic interest in the CJ succession question.

The paradox of Function 3 (Passionate Reformer): the CJ must interact with public and private offices, foreign governments, and international institutions to keep the judiciary current with the Information Age — 'without arousing public suspicion' — a 'really sensitive balancing act' that makes deep public trust in the CJ's personal integrity the only reliable protection.

Function 8 (Role Model and Exemplar) as the capstone: during periods of 'political wrangling, civic groups and nonpartisan organizations turn to the CJ to grace their seminars and inductions' and 'find solace and peace in his quiet persona' — positioning the CJ as the republic's institutional moral anchor precisely when politics fails.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban draws from his book 'With Due Respect' (printed edition sold out) to enumerate the eight unique functions of the chief justice not required of associate justices. Beyond the constitutional qualifications (natural-born, at least 40, 15 years as judge or lawyer, proven competence, integrity, probity, independence), the CJ must be: (1) primus inter pares -- presiding over sessions and shaping the SC's agenda with only one vote, relying entirely on moral ascendancy; (2) leader of the entire judiciary -- CEO of 2,000 lower court judges and 26,000 employees; (3) passionate reformer -- interacting with public and private offices, foreign governments, and international institutions while maintaining integrity 'without arousing public suspicion'; (4) leader of the bar -- guiding lawyers as the institutional head of law practice supervision; (5) academic and maestro -- ex-officio chair of the Philippine Judicial Academy; (6) mover and shaker -- as JBC chair, securing better compensation and facilities to attract the best and brightest to the judiciary; (7) administrator, manager and finance wizard -- wielding 'exclusive sole power' to disburse the JDF and SAJ funds under PD 1949 and RA 9227; and (8) role model and exemplar -- during political turmoil, civic groups 'find solace and peace in his quiet persona.' The CJ, he concludes, is more accurately the 'Chief Justice of the Philippines,' not merely of the Supreme Court.
